newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian non-bank mortgage share growing - PUMA.
newsitem.headline: Australian non-bank mortgage share growing - PUMA.

text.p: Non-bank lenders' market share of Australia's increasingly competitive mortgage market continues to grow, said Australia's largest mortgage securitisation business, PUMA Management Ltd.
"Market shares of the non-bank lenders over the last three months has been growing at 17.5 percent," said Frank Ganis, deputy managing director of PUMA, Macquarie Bank Ltd's securitisation arm.
"With non-bank lenders, particularly Aussie Home Loans, now established and reliable alternatives to the banks, this trend is expected to continue," Ganis told a conference in Sydney.

Speaking at an International Communications for Management seminar Ganis said that dissatisfaction with the major banks' failure to pass on the full impact of official interest rate cuts to home loan customers has provided non-bank lenders with further opportunities in the home mortgage market.
He said that enquiries for home loan refinancing had risen substantially since the Reserve Bank cut official interest rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent on May 23.
"The changes in the market are structural rather than seasonal and participants who fail to achieve a speedy reduction in costs will not survive," Ganis said.

Ganis said there is also an overwhelming consumer desire to remove their business from traditional bank lenders which, because of the pressure on profit margins, have been unable to match the rates of the non-banks.

"Consumers are suspicious of banks and what they may do in the future to recover the margins foregone over recent times. Not passing on the full 0.5 percentage point rate reduction and introduction of fees has undone any goodwill the banks have built up," Ganis said.
He added that non-bank lenders must continue to create innovative market lending products to cement their rapidly growing share of the Australian mortgage market.
